findings.summary: The rule scoped to engine-gmt/features/** + engine-gmt/store/** — titled 'engine-gmt feature catalog + camera manager' — cites npm run smoke:camera as its guard, but that smoke boots fluid-toy.html, which never imports either path, so no change in the rule's scope can make it fail.

findings.verification: Two-sided. (1) The replacement is real and green: smoke:statelibrary-drop passed all three assertions, and its assertions are on app-gmt's Camera Manager savedCameras list — exactly the camera_manager + installStateLibrary surface the rule names. It would fail if row reorder or the state-library slice regressed. (2) The removed citation is provably blind: smoke:camera was ALSO run and passed, but its entry point is fluid-toy.html (smoke-camera.mts:11) and every assertion reads s.julia / s.setJulia plus window.__camera from engine/plugins/Camera.ts. `grep -rn 'engine-gmt' fluid-toy/` returns 7 hits, all engine-gmt/support or engine-gmt/feedback — none under features/ or store/. Since those modules are not in fluid-toy's import graph, no edit within the rule's scope can be observed by that smoke. Sixth instance this run of the 'healthy but cited for the wrong thing' mode.

findings.verification: The counts are a runtime measurement, not a reading. A probe calls registerFeatures() then featureRegistry.getAll() and prints 'registered features: 27' plus the full id list; six of those resolve to ../../engine/features/* imports and the other 21 to ./-relative engine-gmt paths, which is the grep that proves the section labels wrong. test:param-mapping was run AFTER the edit and passes — it imports and executes this exact file's registerFeatures() then walks every feature's params, so it would fail loudly if registration were disturbed. The registry sweep was re-run after the edit and still reports 27 with only the two pre-existing owner-queued collisions. Worth noting the causal link recorded in the commit: a reader who trusts those headers draws the opposite conclusion from the truth about module identity, which is a plausible reason the droste/drawing collision went unnoticed — nobody cross-checks an alias against a def they believe lives in engine-core.

notes:
ELEVEN REGISTRY-WIDE SWEEPS RUN over the live registry after registerFeatures() (27 features). A proven-clean sweep is a real result, so all are recorded:

1. FEATURE-LEVEL shortId uniqueness, global — computed with the real `feat.shortId || feat.id` fallback getDictionary uses. Exactly ONE collision: `dr` <- droste, drawing. The already-queued Tier B bug; NO OTHERS EXIST.
2. PARAM-LEVEL shortId uniqueness within each of the 27 — exactly ONE: materials `ec` <- envMapColorSpace, emissionMode. Again the known one; NO OTHERS. This confirms the @bug PRODUCTION note in engine/FeatureSystem.ts is COMPLETE rather than a sample — worth knowing before the owner picks a wire-format fix.
3. UNIFORM-NAME uniqueness across the whole GLSL namespace (every param with a `uniform:` field, all 27) — ZERO collisions. Two features writing one uniform would be a silent last-writer-wins render bug; proven clean.
4. dependsOn integrity — every declared dependency names a registered feature AND sorts earlier in getAll()'s topological order. ZERO problems; the LightSpheres-after-Lighting invariant holds at runtime.
5. Params with no default — ZERO.
6. Vestigial fields the CLAUDE.md anti-patterns list calls out (defaultActive, aggregatesFrom, tabConfig.dock) — ZERO present. That anti-pattern is fully cleaned up.
7. Dangling condition.param / parentId references — 2 flagged, BOTH false positives, so genuinely ZERO. atmosphere.fogTint uses `$materials.envSource` and materials.ptEmissionMult uses `$renderMode`; both use the documented `$`-prefix global-state escape and both resolve.
8. Params lacking a shortId (silently absent from every share link) — 5, ALL correct: geometry's preRot/postRot/worldRot/julia are composeFrom derived vec3s whose scalar sources carry their own shortIds, and drawing.refreshTrigger is a hidden system nonce that must not serialise.
9. Panel-manifest cross-check over engine-gmt/panels.ts — all 15 compileParam / runtimeToggleParam / compileSettingsParams references resolve to a real param on the named feature. ZERO dangling; a dangling one would mean a compile gate that never fires.
10. Rule coverage — every path under engine-gmt/features/** is matched by at least gmt-features.md and fork-rules.md; fragmentarium_import additionally by scene-and-formula-format.md. NO coverage gap of the kind cycle 5 found in engine/components/. All four scripts cited by gmt-features.md exist; the defect was the entry point of one, reported as finding 1.
11. holdsLiveSession — only `audio` declares it, across all 27. Consistent with the cycle-1 handoff.

FEATURES NOT OPENED (swept programmatically, bodies never read): ao, coloring, lighting/index.ts, lighting/light_spheres.ts, optics, navigation, quality, reflections, texturing, volumetric, water_plane, weave, core_math, camera_manager/logic.ts, camera_manager/CameraManagerPanel.tsx, rotation_gizmo, engine/ (shaderCompiler + profiles), and the ENTIRE fragmentarium_import subtree (FormulaWorkshop, parsers/, v3/, v4/, transform/ — by far the largest, completely unaudited here).
